problem: The three-dimensional rule given is wrong/ambiguous: "curl the fingers from the first force toward the second, and the thumb gives the couple vector." The two forces of a couple are antiparallel, so there is no unique way to curl from one to the other, and a student following this can get the opposite sense.
fix: The couple vector is perpendicular to the plane of the two forces. Its sense is fixed by the right-hand rule: curl the fingers in the sense in which the couple tends to rotate the body, and the thumb gives the couple vector. (Looking along the vector, the couple turns the body counterclockwise.)

problem: "the same 72 N·m clockwise couple is the moment about any other point of the plate; only the force at that other point would change" is wrong and contradicts Q6. If the translation is made to another point O', the force vector is unchanged, but the couple becomes r' × F, which is not 72 N·m. Only a couple by itself has the same moment about every point; a force-couple system does not.
fix: Check: the couple in this system is a free vector, so its 72 N·m bending effect can be drawn anywhere. But the couple belongs to the force-couple system: if the force is translated to a different point O', the force stays 120 N downward and the couple changes to r' × F, because the moment arm from O' to A is different.

problem: "The position terms cancel in pairs, and the sum is still F d" skips the actual step. The two position terms do not cancel to zero; they combine into one term.
fix: Write the moments about P as (r₁ − r_P) × F + (r₂ − r_P) × (−F) = (r₁ − r₂) × F. The term in r_P drops out, so the result is F d and does not depend on P.

problem: "a force and a couple at a point are packaged as a wrench" is loose. A general force plus couple reduces to a wrench only after a suitable choice of point; a wrench is a force together with a couple parallel to that force.
fix: Any force-couple system can be reduced, at a suitable point, to a single force plus a couple parallel to it; this six-number package is called a wrench.
